0.why: JTKeys.cpp:136 sets this output's channel count from the highest key channel in use; JTKeys.cpp:127 writes one pitch per channel

1.why: JTKeys.cpp:137 sets this output's channel count; JTKeys.cpp:134 writes 10V or 0V

2.why: JTKeys.cpp:138 sets this output's channel count; JTKeys.cpp:131-133 hold it at 10V except during a one millisecond pulse

comment: The output named Trig is high while a key is held and drops for one millisecond each time a key is switched on, JTKeys.cpp:129-133, which is the opposite way round from an ordinary trigger. The pulse generator is shared by all sixteen channels, so two keys pressed together give one dip. The module has no inputs at all: it is played by clicking. The ninety-three key switches are named by the ratios of the first scale in the file, JTKeys.cpp:75, so their tooltips do not follow the Scales knob.
